epic.intent:
Users have no way to get rid of an epic, and removing a ticket today takes Edit draft → open ticket → Remove ticket… → Save. Add a real delete for both, from the desktop app.

**Epic delete is a hard delete.** It removes every database row for the epic (revisions, draft, ticket statuses, runs and their attempts/reports/checkpoints/grants, approvals, comments, events, search index, sync state, pending outbox entries) and deletes `.darkmechanicus/epics/<id>/` and the `.darkmechanicus/history/<runId>/` folder of each of its runs. It never commits; the person commits the removal. It is refused while the epic has an active run (queued, running, awaiting checkpoint, paused). Completed epics can be deleted.

**Ticket delete is one click from the saved view.** It removes the ticket (and its dependency edges and relations) from the current saved plan and saves a new revision in one step. It is refused when the draft holds unsaved changes, when the epic is completed, when a save is still pending, or when the ticket has an open attempt (claimed, running, submitted).

Both are desktop-only (human) capabilities; no agent role receives them.

successCriteria.text: A desktop session can hard-delete an epic: afterwards no table references it, its `.darkmechanicus/epics/<id>/` and its runs' `.darkmechanicus/history/<runId>/` folders are gone, and a reconcile does not bring it back
Deleting an epic with an active run fails with `active_run_exists` and changes nothing
A desktop session can delete a ticket from the saved view in one action, producing a new saved revision without the ticket, its edges or relations
Ticket delete is refused, changing nothing, when the draft has unsaved changes, the epic is completed, a save is pending, or the ticket has an open attempt
No agent role (planner, orchestrator, worker, reviewer) holds the delete capabilities, even with --allow-save
lint, test, fireguard, typecheck, deadcode and build all pass

epic.title: Delete epics and tickets from the desktop app

bundle.rationale: Core commands first so the UI tickets build on a tested API. Epic and ticket tracks are independent and can run in parallel. One sprint: the work is small and each UI ticket only needs its core ticket.

exitCriteria.text: Full verification gate passes on the combined change

sprints.goal: Hard-delete epics and one-click delete tickets, end to end from core to desktop UI

acceptanceCriteria.text: A test deletes an epic that has a saved revision, a draft, a finished run with attempts/report/checkpoint, and comments, then asserts zero rows reference the epic id or its run ids in every table
The same test asserts `.darkmechanicus/epics/<id>/` and `.darkmechanicus/history/<runId>/` no longer exist, and `reconcileRepository` afterwards does not recreate the epic
A test shows delete with an active run fails with `active_run_exists` and leaves rows and files untouched
A test shows only the desktop role holds `epic.delete` (planner/orchestrator with allowSave, worker, reviewer do not), and a non-desktop call fails with `unauthorized`

tickets.body:
**In scope**
- New human-only capability `epic.delete` in `src/core/authz.ts` (`CAPABILITIES`, `HUMAN_ONLY_CAPABILITIES`; desktop gets it, no agent role does).
- New `deleteEpic({ epicId })` on `CommandApi` (`src/shared/domain/api.ts`), schema in `src/core/commandSchemas.ts`, entry in `src/core/commands/capabilities.ts` and `src/core/commands/authoring.ts`. Not exposed as an MCP tool.
- Service in `src/core/services/epics.ts` (or a new `epicDeletion.ts`): in one transaction, refuse with `active_run_exists` when `activeRun()` returns a run, otherwise delete children before parents (foreign keys are on): attempts, retry_grants, sprint_reports, checkpoints (by run), approvals, runs, ticket_status, comments, drafts, plan_revisions, events, search_index, sync_state (epic, its runs, its comments), outbox rows for the epic, its runs and its comments, then the epic row.
- After commit, remove `.darkmechanicus/epics/<id>/` and each run's `.darkmechanicus/history/<runId>/` with `ownedPaths` + `assertContained` (no links followed). `FsAdapter` gains `removeDir` (empty directory only) in `src/core/repo/types.ts`, `nodeFs.ts`, and `src/test/memoryFs.ts`.
- Never commits to git.

**Out of scope**: UI, ticket delete, soft delete/archive.

**Verify**: Vitest service and command tests using the in-memory fs; a reconcile after delete must not re-import the epic.
tickets.title: Add a desktop-only deleteEpic command that hard-deletes an epic and its portable files

acceptanceCriteria.text: A test deletes a ticket that has dependency edges and relations from a saved plan; after flush the epic's current saved revision lacks the ticket, its edges and its relations, and the revision number went up by one
Tests show refusal, with no new revision, for: draft with unsaved changes, completed epic, pending save, ticket with an open attempt, unknown ticket
A test shows an unchanged draft (Edit draft with no edits) does not block delete
A test shows only the desktop role holds `ticket.delete`

tickets.body:
**In scope**
- New human-only capability `ticket.delete` in `src/core/authz.ts` (desktop only).
- New `deleteTicket({ epicId, ticketId })` on `CommandApi`, schema, capability-table entry, command in `src/core/commands/authoring.ts`. Not an MCP tool.
- Service (in `src/core/services/plans.ts` or `tickets.ts`): load the epic, `assertEpicOpen`, `ctx.assertBranch()`, refuse if a save is pending, refuse if a draft exists whose content differs from the saved revision, refuse if the ticket has an attempt in `claimed|running|submitted`; apply the existing `remove_ticket` draft op (`src/core/plan/draftOps.ts`) to the current saved bundle, validate, and record a pending revision the same way `requestSave` does (snapshot outbox entry; the finalizer completes it). Drop an unchanged draft so it does not go stale.
- A never-saved epic has no saved view: refuse with a clear message (the draft editor's Remove ticket… covers it).

**Out of scope**: UI, epic delete, changing the existing draft-only Remove ticket… flow.

**Verify**: Vitest service tests.
tickets.title: Add a desktop-only deleteTicket command that removes a ticket from the saved plan and saves a new revision

tickets.body:
**In scope**
- Allow-list `deleteEpic` in `DESKTOP_COMMANDS` (`src/shared/desktop/api.ts`).
- A `Delete epic…` control in the epic workspace header (`src/renderer/src/epic/WorkspaceHeader.tsx`), using the existing confirm flow (`ws.dispatch({ type: 'confirm', kind: ... })`). The confirm text says it deletes the epic, its runs and history, and the files under `.darkmechanicus/` (uncommitted).
- On success, the epic leaves the sidebar list and the app navigates away from it; on failure (e.g. active run) the error message shows.

**Out of scope**: core logic, ticket delete UI.

**Verify**: renderer tests (Testing Library) for confirm, cancel, success navigation, and error display.

tickets.body:
**In scope**
- Allow-list `deleteTicket` in `DESKTOP_COMMANDS`.
- A `Delete ticket…` control in the saved-view ticket panel (`src/renderer/src/ticket/TicketPanel.tsx`) with an inline confirm like the draft editor's `RemoveTicket`. Hidden for completed epics.

**Out of scope**: core logic, the draft editor's existing Remove ticket…, epic delete UI.

**Verify**: renderer tests.
